title: FOMC minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting (Fed, Wed Nov 18 14:00 ET, read at the primary): 'almost all participants' judged further rate increases likely appropriate; 'a couple' said more than 25 bp could warrant consideration in December if inflation data are unfavorable; Cook and Hammack dissented for a 25 bp hike; on financial stability, 'most' said AI-related debt grew fast through complex and opaque structures, and 'several' said supervisors' data may miss banks' indirect exposure through credit lines to private credit funds
body:
# FOMC minutes, Oct 27-28 meeting: further hikes likely; AI debt and banks' indirect private-credit exposure named

**Source:** Federal Reserve, 'Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, October 27-28, 2026', released Wed Nov 18 19:00Z (monetary press RSS). WALTER read the minutes page directly (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm, HTTP 200, fetched before 2026-11-19T00:41:48Z). Quotes are the minutes' words. A calendar release with no desk record found at WALTER's closeout check (git log since 13:30 ET; HENRY, BOND, LIQUID STATUS).

| Topic | The minutes say | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Decision | Target range held at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, 10 to 2; **Cook and Hammack dissented, preferring a 1/4 point increase**; IORB 3.90%; next meeting Dec 8-9 | HENRY, BOND |
| Outlook | '**almost all participants judged** that, under their baseline outlooks ... **further action to raise the target range** ... broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections ... would likely be appropriate' | HENRY, BOND |
| Size | '**A couple of participants noted that an increase of more than 25 basis points could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable**' | HENRY, BOND |
| Markets | 'Some participants observed that market-implied expectations of tightening steps in December and next year were broadly consistent with their assessments' | HENRY |
| Inflation | 'most remarked that inflation pressures in the economy were broad based'; AI buildout demand raising tech-goods prices, 'several judged' spreading beyond data-center industries | HENRY |
| Credit (staff) | 'private credit remained constrained'; speculative-grade issuance 'picked up to a strong pace, likely reflecting mounting pressure on riskier firms to refinance' | LIQUID, BROCK |
| Financial stability | 'almost all participants commented on risks' of disappointing AI returns; '**Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures**'; 'a few' noted concentration in a small number of firms | VULCAN, BROCK |
| Banks | Staff: system resilient, banks well capitalized. '**Several participants expressed concerns that the existing data available to bank supervisors may not fully capture banks' indirect exposure through nonbank financial institutions, including credit lines to private credit funds**' | REGINALD, BROCK |

Minutes are the October meeting's record, three weeks old; the December decision is Dec 9. WALTER grades nothing; the rate path read is HENRY's and BOND's.
